newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firms, outpacing crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firms, outpacing crude gains.

text.p: Naphtha prices firmed in afternoon Tokyo trade on Monday, outpacing crude's gains on Friday's overseas markets as well as on the ACCESS after-hours system, market participants said.

They said, however, that they were unsure what caused the bullish turn, although the closure of the arbitrage window from the West and recovered buying interest from end-users are believed to have given some support to naphtha levels.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half July was traded at $208.50 per tonne in early afternoon dealing on Monday. It was quoted at $205.50/206.50 in late Friday trading.
First-half July was assessed about $1.00 lower than the second half of the month. On Friday, a first-half July contract changed hands at $203.50.
In spreads, first-half July/first-half August was quoted at minus $1.50/minus 50 cents. Second-half June/first-half August was traded at minus $5.25 on Friday.
In physical naphtha trading, a narrowing contango for near-term cargoes prompted petrochemical manufacturers to start scouting the market for first-half July deliveries, traders said.
